text:
olivia: FYI, JunoPay is escalating — their contract-summarizer endpoint is inserting made-up clauses and future termination dates after the runtime change we rolled this morning. They say summaries now mention warranty periods and exact termination dates that are not in the source PDF.
cs-bot: Customer excerpt: "We uploaded a 2-page supplier contract and the summary suddenly lists a '3-year warranty' and a termination date of 2027-12-31. Those phrases are not in the contract. This is blocking our compliance review." Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/JP-4211
deploy-bot: Deployed runtime toggle: `decoder-merge-v2` enabled in canary at 2024-10-14T09:43:21Z by sam (commit abc123def) — deploy id: dply-20241014-01
sam: tagging @eng-ml — initial hunch: decoder selection change may have increased insertion bias during decoding.
leo: can you paste the raw request/response and model name + params? need a minimal repro.
olivia: minimal repro (customer provided):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/summarize \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-summarizer-1.0","input":"<redacted contract text>","max_tokens":300}'
```
Old (pre-deploy) summary: "No warranty beyond 90 days. No termination date specified."
New (post-deploy) summary: "Includes a 3-year warranty and termination date 2027-12-31."
maria: got the customer's request ids: rq_8f9a (2278455001) and rq_8f9b (2278455010). They attached the original contract.
eng-ml: can you confirm model_version and tokenizer hash used in prod? also any runtime flags (beam, temp, top_p)?
sam: prod config: model=redwood-summarizer-1.0@v1.7.2, tokenizer_hash=tok-hash-4b2, decoding_toggle=decoder-merge-v2 (canary enabled). No explicit beam, temp=0.0, top_p=0.95.
leo: I'm running local repro against the same model commit (abc123def) with default decoder — local run returns the correct summary (no warranty/date). Trying prod runtime image now: image rtd-2024-10-14-abc123.
eng-ml: quick update — reproduces when using `decoder-merge-v2` on the prod runtime image. Observed decoding tail behavior that occasionally inserts tokens like 'warranty' and date tokens. Attached short logits excerpt below for comparison:
```
old_decoder top tokens: ["no", "warranty", "beyond", ...] (stable low-prob for 'warranty')
new_decoder top tokens: ["includes", "3-year", "warranty", ...] (heavier tail; insertion spikes around clause boundaries)
```
olivia: customer flagged this as a compliance/regulatory risk and requested immediate mitigation.
sam: can we roll the canary toggle back? Prefer fast rollback if safe.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: `decoder-merge-v2` toggle disabled by sam at 2024-10-14T09:53:40Z (action id rbk-20241014-02).
maria: notified JunoPay that we're investigating and rolling back; they're waiting for confirmation before resuming reviews. :thumbsup:
eng-ml: root cause summary: `decoder-merge-v2` changes decoder combination weights causing an insertion bias on mid-length structured docs. Plan: 1) rollback (done), 2) AB test decoding params, 3) patch decoder merge to avoid token insertion at clause boundaries, 4) add regression tests around contractual clause hallucinations.
leo: I'm creating a deterministic repro harness using the customer's exact input and token stream so QA can validate the hotfix.
olivia: please keep CS updated; if rollback doesn't fully resolve, escalate to legal/compliance and prepare a customer-facing summary.
eng-ml: noted — will post follow-ups with fixed experiments and ETA for patch.
